newsitem.title: USA: Hilton shareholders approve Bally merger.
newsitem.headline: Hilton shareholders approve Bally merger.

text.p: Shareholders of Hilton Hotels Corp., the giant hotel chain, on Thursday approved the company's $3 billion merger with gambling company Bally Entertainment Corp.

Hilton also installed Bally Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Arthur Goldberg at the helm of its gambling operations as an executive vice president of Hilton Hotels and president of the gaming division.

The acquisition, valued at $3 billion including the assumption of debt, makes Hilton the largest hotel and gambling concern in the United States, with 16 casinos in cities like Las Vegas, Atlantic City, N.J., New Orleans and Reno, Nev.
The combined company will have 18,000 rooms in hotel/casinos and 100,000 hotel rooms overall.
"It's difficult to imagine a more dominant force in the gaming business," Hilton Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach, told shareholders at a special meeting to vote on the merger.
The acquisition included a four-for-one stock split, which was also approved, and afterward, Hilton said it would raise its annual dividend by 6.7 percent to 8 cents a share.
Hilton stock rose $1.125 to $106.75 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
Changes are planned for the merged operations. In Atlantic City, Bally's hotel called The Grand will likely be renamed with the Hilton brand.
In Las Vegas, Hilton will continue to develop the huge 3,000-room Bally "Paris" hotel for an opening in 1998 with no changes to its current design.
The acquisition and deal-making spree Hilton has been on since Bollenbach came on board in February will not end with the Bally deal.
Hilton will continue to acquire major hotel operations, and Bollenbach said there are currently "substantive" talks in that area. He declined to name companies he was looking at.
On the gambling side, any acquisitions are not likely to occur until after the Bally deal is completed.
